title: Ajay Mohan Pathak v. State of U.P.
principles: Citation and adaptation of New Zealand family law principles (Walker & Harrison) in assessing family welfare and spousal support standards.
summary: High Court examined comparative jurisprudence from Commonwealth jurisdictions (New Zealand) to interpret the standard of living and equitable maintenance for abandoned spouses in transnational marriages.

title: Ajit Datt v. Ethel Walters
principles: Evidentiary verification of marriage status, valid solemnization, and church/ecclesiastical documentation for Christian marriage maintenance disputes.
summary: Reiterates evidentiary thresholds for proving valid solemnization of Christian marriages before adjudicating pendente lite and permanent alimony.

title: Alla Venkata Sanath Babji Reddy v. Government of A.P.
principles: International child custody, inter-parental relocation, and comity of foreign courts versus paramount welfare of the minor child.
summary: Held that foreign custody orders are not automatically enforceable in India without independent inquiry into the best interest and welfare of the child.

title: Amit Jalan v. State of West Bengal
principles: Lump-sum permanent alimony settlement (Rs 3.5 crores) deposited in court enables mutual divorce under Section 13B HMA and quashing of all pending matrimonial litigation.
summary: Demonstrates the judicial framework for structuring comprehensive multi-crore permanent alimony escrow settlements in high-net-worth matrimonial disputes.

title: Angalakurthy Venkata Narayanamma v. Lakshmamma
principles: Comparative application of international law principles (UK ECHR jurisprudence) regarding property division and matrimonial rights.
summary: Applies international human rights and equitable property distribution benchmarks to resolve domestic maintenance and residence claims.

title: Anita Sharma v. Shiv Onkar
principles: Concealment of true earning capacity justifies drawing compulsory adverse inference on income against overseas spouse.
summary: Established that when an NRI husband suppresses his foreign pay slips, tax filings, or bank statements, courts must draw adverse inference and impute high earning capacity.

title: Anju v. Sonu
principles: Able-bodied NRI husband cannot take the plea of claimed unemployment or visa expiry to evade maintenance obligations to wife and child.
summary: Affirmed the Anju Garg principle in transnational settings: an able-bodied spouse is presumed capable of earning and supporting dependents regardless of overseas job switches.

title: B.P. Badrinath v. Lata Badrinath
principles: Assessment of overseas professional income, execution of maintenance warrants through diplomatic channels and MEA against defaulting NRI husband.
summary: Laid down execution protocols for recovering maintenance arrears from NRI spouses working in Gulf jurisdictions through consular channels.

title: Baiju v. Hema
principles: Compulsory adverse inference when NRI husband fails to disclose foreign monthly income and offshore bank balances.
summary: Landmark Kerala HC precedent establishing that failure by an NRI spouse to provide a comprehensive income affidavit justifies presuming income at standard foreign market rates.

title: Balvinder Singh v. Suman Rani
principles: Spouse relocating abroad on student/work visa without mutual consent or abandoning the other in India constitutes statutory desertion under HMA.
summary: Clarified that overseas departure under student visa pretext without intention to return or maintain communication qualifies as legal desertion.

title: Basheer v. Sahira
principles: Irretrievable breakdown is not a statutory ground under HMA Sec 13 or personal laws unless enacted by legislature; cannot be invoked to deny maintenance.
statutes: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986
summary: Held that emotional estrangement or long overseas stay does not extinguish statutory liability to provide reasonable and fair maintenance.

title: Beatrice v. Babu Louis
principles: Revision of maintenance quantum awarded to wife and children considering Gulf earnings and rising standard of living.
summary: Affirmed revision of maintenance quantum under Section 127 CrPC to reflect increased school fees, medical expenses, and husband's upgraded foreign package.

title: Biju P. John v. Priya Syriac
principles: Evaluation of husband's actual earning capacity against claims of meagre local income when holding overseas qualifications and employment history.
summary: Rejected husband's contention of low domestic earnings when his resume, foreign work visa, and professional credentials established substantial earning power.

title: Chittibomma Veera Venkata Raju v. Sakuntala
principles: Dissolution of marriage does not extinguish wife's statutory right to permanent alimony under Section 25 HMA; quantum tied to standard of living.
summary: Enforces lifetime financial security under Section 25 HMA even where marriage was dissolved on grounds of mutual incompatibility.

title: Darshan Singh v. State of Punjab
principles: Issuance of non-bailable warrants and proclamation under Section 82/83 CrPC against NRI husband evading maintenance and domestic violence trial.
summary: Established coercive criminal process parameters to impound property and compel presence of non-resident defendants.

title: Deepak Nenawati v. Kavita Nenawati
principles: Assessment of interim maintenance under Section 24 HMA during pendency of overseas litigation; spouse entitled to live according to husband's status.
summary: Mandates that interim maintenance must enable the dependent spouse to maintain parity with the affluent status enjoyed by the overseas partner.

title: Deepamala Mohan v. State of Telangana
principles: Grant of interim maintenance under Section 125 CrPC pending main trial; non-payment results in striking off defense in matrimonial proceedings.
summary: Strengthened judicial sanction: an NRI spouse who defaults on interim maintenance orders faces having his defense struck off.

title: Wilson Raj Palanna v. State & Smt. Dina Susan
principles: Territorial jurisdiction under DV Act Section 27 where aggrieved wife resides or takes temporary shelter in India after abandonment abroad.
summary: Affirmed that an Indian court has complete jurisdiction under Section 27 DV Act wherever the abandoned wife takes shelter in India, even if domestic violence occurred abroad.

title: Fathima Majida M. v. Union of India
principles: Passport re-issuance and removal of spouse name following foreign decree cannot be arbitrarily blocked by administrative circulars without Section 13 CPC scrutiny.
summary: Key guidance on passport impoundment and renewal: clarifies legal limits between executive discretion and court declaratory decrees under Section 13 CPC.

title: Gangadhara Panicker Bhuvanendran v. Sreeja
category: DV Act Shared Household & Overseas Absence
principles: Aggrieved woman's right to reside in shared household protected under Section 17/19 DV Act even when husband is working abroad.
summary: Confirmed that the physical absence of the husband abroad does not permit in-laws or the husband to dispossess the wife from the matrimonial home.

title: Gopal Singh Visharad v. Zahoor Ahmad
principles: Principles governing preservation of subject matter and maintenance of status quo in family and religious dispute properties.
summary: Procedural benchmark on preserving matrimonial property from alienation prior to final alimony adjudication.

title: Hemavathi Shivashankar v. Dr. Tumkur S. Shivashankar
principles: Husband relocates to USA and obtains foreign ex-parte decree; Indian court retains jurisdiction to award maintenance and evaluate matrimonial assets.
summary: Direct ruling that migration to the United States and obtaining an overseas decree does not wipe out statutory maintenance liabilities in India.

title: Israr Ahmad v. Azazul Hussain Ahmad
principles: Examination of bank remittances from Gulf countries to determine actual monthly income for maintenance calculation.
summary: Ruled that regular foreign remittances received in domestic NRE/NRO accounts are conclusive prima facie evidence of overseas earning capacity.

title: Jasdev Singh v. Rajwinder Kaur
principles: Husband residing in Auckland, New Zealand; Indian court has jurisdiction under Section 19 HMA based on wife's permanent residence.
summary: Affirmed venue under HMA 19(iii-a) favoring the wife's place of residence when husband is settled abroad in New Zealand.

title: Jasvir Singh v. State of Punjab
principles: Interim litigation expenses and monthly pendente lite maintenance must reflect international travel and legal defense expenses incurred by wife.
summary: Awarded enhanced litigation expenses acknowledging the asymmetrical burden on an Indian spouse fighting legal battles against an overseas partner.

title: Kulsam Beevi v. State of Kerala
principles: Reference to US 9th Circuit Court of Appeals precedents on child removal and international parental custody.
summary: Emphasizes comity of courts while prioritizing the protection of dependent children residing in India.

title: Kulwinder Kumar v. Seema
principles: Sets mandatory interim maintenance floor for NRI husbands; minimum ₹10,000 to ₹25,000/pm baseline even where exact income is unproven.
summary: Landmark benchmark setting an irrebuttable interim maintenance floor against NRI spouses who stonewall financial disclosures.

title: Mohd. Fazil Qureshi v. State of M.P.
principles: Enhancement of monthly maintenance quantum considering inflation, rising consumer price index, and husband's overseas business growth.
summary: Formulated periodic indexation principle: maintenance awards must be adjusted upward every 2-3 years to offset inflation and cost of living surges.

title: Moideenkutty v. Subaida
category: Foreign Property & Abu Dhabi Commercial Assets
principles: Maintenance under Sec 125 CrPC considering husband's employment and commercial property holdings in Abu Dhabi.
summary: Held that offshore commercial properties and business ownership in UAE can be evaluated through audited returns and trade licenses to quantify maintenance.

title: Muneeba Shamsudeen v. Mohd. Safeek
principles: Claim for monthly maintenance allowance under Section 125 CrPC against overseas husband residing in Gulf; currency conversion standards.
summary: Addresses the conversion of AED/SAR currency to INR without arbitrary devaluation, ensuring the child's living standard mirrors the father's earnings.

title: Nitaben v. Dhirendra Chandrakant Shukla
principles: Assessment of husband's income who is employed abroad; consideration of foreign currency exchange rate and higher local cost of living.
summary: Pioneering Gujarat HC judgment creating the doctrine of foreign living expense deduction before converting overseas salary to Indian currency.

title: Noushad Flourish v. Akhila Flourish
principles: Plea regarding foreign domicile in Tanzania does not defeat jurisdiction of Family Court in India where marriage was solemnized.
summary: Explicitly held that acquiring foreign citizenship or permanent residency in Tanzania does not oust the jurisdiction of Indian courts over personal law remedies.

title: Parul Tyagi v. Gaurav Tyagi
principles: Husband working in Qatar failed to disclose salary certificate; court applied adverse inference and enhanced interim maintenance.
summary: Mandated that where a professional employed in Qatar conceals compensation, the court will rely on industry averages in Doha to fix maintenance.

title: Prabhu v. State of Karnataka
principles: Court empowered to draw adverse inference and assume higher financial capacity upon willful non-disclosure of overseas income tax returns.
summary: Reinforces that transparency in filing the Supreme Court mandated affidavit of assets and liabilities is mandatory, non-compliance being fatal.

title: Priyam Malik nee Jatua v. Biplab Malik
principles: Ex-parte divorce under Special Marriage Act obtained through dubious summons service while wife was pregnant and traveling from Dubai set aside.
summary: Vigorously protected the right of an overseas mother against clandestine ex-parte divorce decrees obtained without proper international service.

title: Ravi Shankar v. State of Bihar
principles: Procedures for serving summons through Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) and Indian embassies abroad in maintenance execution cases.
summary: Outlines statutory protocol under Section 105 CrPC for reciprocal summons service on overseas respondents through embassy liaisons.

title: Reena v. State of Rajasthan
principles: Comparative judicial analysis referencing Western Australia, New Zealand, and Indian DV Acts for protective injunctions.
summary: Synthesizes Australian restraining order standards into Indian domestic violence orders to restrain transnational harassment.

title: Rupa C. v. Puthalath Anil Kumar
principles: Wife relocated to New Zealand on study visa while husband stayed in India; examination of constructive desertion versus mutual career advancement.
summary: Distinguished between genuine career relocation with consent and willful abandonment intended to bring cohabitation to an end.

title: Satya v. Teja Singh
principles: Nevada divorce decree obtained by husband on fleeting residence is a fraud on jurisdiction under Section 13 CPC; marital tie subsists and maintenance continues.
summary: Foundational Supreme Court precedent: Indian citizens married under Hindu law cannot be stripped of maintenance rights via quick-divorce decrees obtained from foreign jurisdictions without bona fide domicile.

title: Sehadri Satvik Desai v. Satvik Gautam Desai
principles: Interpretation of statutory disqualification under Section 125(4) CrPC; wife living separately due to domestic abuse or abandonment abroad is entitled to maintenance.
summary: Held that a wife forced to return to India due to overseas domestic cruelty has 'sufficient reason' to live separately and is never disqualified under Section 125(4).

title: Shereef v. Safna Shamsudheen
principles: Enhancement of monthly maintenance under Section 127 CrPC based on proved career promotions and increased salary in the UAE.
summary: Approved revision of maintenance to ₹35,000/month after establishing husband's progression into senior managerial role in Dubai.

title: Shikha v. Avaneesh Mahodaya
principles: Interim maintenance calculation for overseas spouse (Dubai/Singapore) with standard living expense deduction of 40-50% from gross foreign salary.
summary: Formulated the modern 50% foreign deduction formula: deduct 50% from gross foreign earnings to account for steep overseas living expenses before converting balance to INR.

title: Sita Devi v. Gopal Saran Narayan Singh
principles: Early benchmark on evaluating income earned abroad and deducting requisite expenditure for foreign maintenance.
summary: Historic pre-independence precedent recognizing cost of living differential between Western capitals and Indian domestic expenditure.

title: Subhi N. v. Sreeraj E.
principles: Matrimonial settlements and recognition of foreign divorce proceedings in Sydney and Kentucky under Section 13 CPC.
summary: Reiterated that foreign decrees delivered by courts lacking consensual or natural jurisdiction under Indian private international law are unenforceable.

title: Vimal Ravi v. Vineetha P. Nair
principles: Direct precedent affirming award of ₹15,000 to ₹25,000/pm interim maintenance for NRI spouse residing in Gulf pending final evidence.
summary: Established rapid interim relief guidelines for wives deserted in India while NRI husband resides in UAE.

title: Paul Tushar Biswas v. Addl. District Judge
principles: Jurisdiction of District Court and Family Court under Section 3(1) and 10 of Indian Divorce Act 1869 in transnational Christian marriages.
summary: Addressed forum convenience and maintainability of dissolution petitions for Christian spouses residing across states or overseas.

title: Moni v. Sujatha
principles: Once marriage is legally dissolved, grounds of prior desertion or mutual consent under Section 125(4) cannot be recycled to deny maintenance to divorced wife.
summary: Critical statutory shield: holds that Section 125(4) bars apply only during marriage; once divorce is decreed, past matrimonial fault cannot block maintenance.

title: Baljinder Singh v. Satinderjit Kaur
principles: Ex-parte divorce obtained from Canadian court on ground not recognized under Hindu Marriage Act cannot dissolve Hindu marriage in India.
summary: Strict enforcement of Section 13(c) CPC: foreign judgments founded on a refusal to recognize the law of India applicable to the parties are null and void.

title: Amritpal Kaur v. Rajinder Singh Gill
principles: Foreign decree of divorce obtained in England without wife submitting to jurisdiction does not bar maintenance petition under Section 125 CrPC in India.
summary: Affirmed that an English court's decree passed against a wife residing in Punjab without personal participation is non-executable and does not extinguish maintenance.

title: A. Ashok Vardhan Reddy v. P. Saritha
citation: 2014 SCC OnLine AP 124 / Crl.R.C. No. 15 of 2014
category: US Foreign Decree & DV Act Proceedings
principles: Domestic Violence Act petition and maintenance claim maintainable in India notwithstanding mutual divorce proceedings initiated in the United States.
summary: Held that pending foreign civil actions in the US cannot bar an aggrieved Indian spouse from invoking summary protective remedies under the DV Act.

title: Rajnesh v. Neha
category: Mandatory Affidavit of Assets and Liabilities
principles: Mandatory filing of comprehensive Affidavit of Assets and Liabilities across all maintenance proceedings, including foreign assets, bank accounts, and IT returns.
summary: The Magna Carta of Indian maintenance jurisprudence: lays down standard disclosure templates for salaried, professional, business, and overseas spouses with strict sanctions.

title: Kalyan Dey Chowdhury v. Rita Dey Chowdhury Nee Nandy
principles: 25% of the net salary/income of the husband is an equitable and reasonable benchmark for maintenance to the deserted wife.
summary: Supreme Court benchmark ruling holding that approximately one-fourth (25%) of the husband's net disposable income is a just baseline for spousal support.

title: Devika Jain v. Rajesh Jain
category: Foreign Cost of Living 50% Deduction Rule
principles: 50% reduction on foreign gross earnings before Indian parity conversion to reflect actual high cost of living, taxation, and shelter abroad.
summary: Direct mathematical authority for applying a 50% discount factor to overseas salaries prior to rupee conversion in matrimonial maintenance.

title: Dushiant Sabharwal v. Santosh Gulati
principles: Evaluation of cost of living differential between metropolitan living standards and Tier-2 cities in calibrating maintenance quantum.
summary: Provides comparative cost of living methodology to adjust maintenance based on where the claimant resides versus the respondent.

title: John George Nechupadom v. State of Kerala
principles: Court can order disclosure of overseas directorships, offshore corporate shareholding, and international properties to determine financial standing.
summary: Affirmed Section 91 CrPC summons powers to order production of documents verifying international company registers and offshore assets.
